ACD Zones — Klimaschutzgebiete

Vienna’s Energieraumplanung (Energy Area Planning, ACD) designates geographic zones where specific heating and energy-system rules apply to buildings.

Layer: ogdwien:ENERGIEPLANERPOGD Provider: Vienna Open Government Data WFS Snapshot date: 2026-05-01 Total zones in this snapshot: 50

Zone types:

Type Legal rule
district_heating Buildings must connect to district heating network
heat_pump Heat-pump installations required; fossil fuel banned
fossil_fuel_ban Existing fossil-fuel heating must be retired

Source columns used from the WFS layer: ERPLABEL (zone ID), ERPTYP (zone type), ERPRECHTSTAT (legal status).

HEALTHY — Clean join: building footprint fully contained in a single zone polygon.

The building centroid falls inside exactly one zone, and the overlap fraction is >= 0.95 (at least 95% of the footprint is covered). This is the most common, unambiguous case — the link is legally unequivocal and the downstream rule lookup is trivial.

N (this snapshot): 32 buildings (6.4% of total).

INFORMATIONAL — Building outside any ACD zone.

The building footprint is valid, geocoding succeeded, and the building is in the official inventory — it simply has no ACD zone overlay at this location. This is information, not corruption. About 93.6% of Vienna buildings fall here.

Distinguish from missing data: the building record is complete; the absence of a zone merely means no ACD energy-planning rule applies to this address. Common on Vienna’s outer districts and undeveloped fringes.

N (this snapshot): 468 buildings (93.6% of total).

AMBIGUOUS — Building footprint spans two or more zones (overlap fraction between 5% and 95%).

The POC uses centroid-based assignment: the building is attributed to whichever zone contains its centroid. However, legal applicability may cover both zones for different parts of the building.

Production fix recommended: Replace the single zone_id with a list-column of all overlapping zones plus their respective overlap fractions, and escalate ambiguous cases (overlap fraction 20%–80%) to manual review.

Sample size (this snapshot): 0 buildings (0% of total).

INSPECT — Building centroid falls inside two or more zone polygons simultaneously.

Two possible explanations:

  1. Legitimate layering: Vienna may designate the same area under multiple rule frameworks simultaneously (e.g., district-heating zone AND a fossil-fuel ban zone covering the same geometry). In this case both rules apply and must be stored.

  2. Data error: Zone polygons that should be mutually exclusive may have overlapping geometries due to digitisation errors. Inspect each case.

The POC reports only the first matched zone. Production must store all overlapping zones as a list-column.

N (this snapshot): 0 buildings (0% of total).

INVESTIGATE — Zones containing zero building centroids.

N orphan zones (this snapshot): 34.

Possible causes:

  • (a) Newly designated zone over undeveloped land — legitimate. The zone designates future development requirements; no current buildings to classify.
  • (b) Inventory snapshot lag — buildings exist physically but are not yet catalogued in the GEBAEUDEOGD inventory. The zone polygon is correct; the building list is incomplete.
  • (c) Zone polygon digitisation error — the polygon was drawn in the wrong location. Inspect against imagery.

Investigate each orphan individually before concluding it is a data error.

No invalid-geometry buildings in this snapshot (N = 0). st_make_valid() was applied during fetch — all footprints passed validation.
PASS — Self-intersecting or otherwise broken polygons.

N invalid buildings (this snapshot): 0.

The join pipeline calls sf::st_make_valid() on all input geometries before performing any spatial operations. If this count is non-zero after that step, document the upstream data issue and report it to the data provider.

Expected in a clean run: 0.

No map for this case — CRS errors are caught at code time, not at render time.

CRS chain used in this POC:
Stage CRS EPSG Purpose
Native WFS data MGI / Austria GK East 31256 Source CRS from data provider
Working (analysis) MGI / Austria Lambert 31287 Area + distance calculations
Display (leaflet) WGS84 4326 Leaflet rendering

A CRS mismatch between buildings and zones causes silent ~100 m offsets in centroid-to-zone intersection — buildings that should be inside a zone appear outside it and vice versa.

Protection: join_buildings_zones() contains an explicit assert that both inputs are in EPSG:31287. If either input differs, the function stops with an informative error before any spatial operation runs:

if (b_crs != CRS_WORKING || z_crs != CRS_WORKING) {
  cli::cli_abort(
    c("Both inputs must be in EPSG:{CRS_WORKING}.",
      "i" = "{.arg buildings} CRS: EPSG:{b_crs}",
      "i" = "{.arg zones} CRS: EPSG:{z_crs}")
  )
}

No map for this case — temporal coverage is a data provenance issue, not a spatial geometry issue.

The pinned snapshot is the contract.

Buildings constructed after 2026-05-01 cannot appear in this analysis regardless of their spatial location. The snapshot date is defined once in R/snapshot.R:

SNAPSHOT_DATE <- "2026-05-01"

To refresh the analysis:

  1. Bump SNAPSHOT_DATE in R/snapshot.R.
  2. Re-run fetch_acd_zones() and fetch_buildings() — these write new Parquet files to inst/extdata/zones_<date>.parquet and inst/extdata/buildings_<date>.parquet.
  3. Re-run join_buildings_zones() to produce the new joined Parquet.
  4. Re-render this dashboard.

Do not compare analysis results across snapshots without accounting for the change in building inventory.

Confusion matrix
Disagreements on the map
Notes
What this cross-validation tests

The City of Vienna already tags every building with an ACD identifier in the ogdwien:GEBAEUDEINFOOGD layer (the ACD field). Our spatial join is an independent computation — we overlay building footprints onto zone polygons geometrically, without consulting the city’s pre-linked field.

Disagreements are interesting findings, not data errors:

  • spatial_only (0 buildings): our spatial join finds a zone, but the city’s ACD field is empty or NA. Possible under-coverage in the city’s pre-linking step.
  • acd_only (468 buildings): the city’s ACD field is populated, but our spatial join finds no overlapping zone. Possible stale zone geometry, or a zone that was present when the city’s field was computed but has since been modified in the WFS layer.

Total agreements in this snapshot: 32 buildings. Total disagreements: 468 buildings.

Sampling caveat: This snapshot covers 500 buildings (out of ~220,000 in Vienna). When n_total is a sample rather than the full inventory, the acd_only count is dominated by a sampling artefact — the city has linked buildings that happen to fall outside our sample window, not a genuine join error. Interpret acd_only counts only in the context of a sample (N = 500 < full inventory).

  • Story 1: The cleanly classified apartment block
  • Story 2: Zone-free outskirts

Building 169419738, constructed 1907, falls entirely within Zone 3/010/1 (004049 — legal status: agree_in_zone).

The centroid-based join assigns this building unambiguously to one zone. Overlap fraction: 0. No manual review required. Downstream the legal rule lookup is a simple table join on zone_id.

Building 169396759 sits in district 01 with no ACD zone designation. The building owner is currently free to install any heating system — no ACD energy-planning rule binds this address as of 2026-05-01.

This is not a data error. The building record is complete (year built: 1875, height: 0 m, address: Bräunerstraße 2). The absence of a zone assignment is a valid, informative outcome. It means: no ACD action required for this property.

  • Story 3: The straddler — half a building, half a rule
  • Story 4: The orphan polygon
  • Story 5: The case of the impossible building

Building 169396759 sits with 0% of its footprint inside zone (none). The remaining 100% lies outside that zone — potentially inside another zone.

POC limitation: The centroid-based join assigns this building to the zone containing its centroid. The reported zone_id is none and the reported link_status is straddles_boundary as a warning signal.

Production fix: Store a list-column of all overlapping zones with individual overlap fractions. Legal teams should handle boundary-straddling buildings case-by-case.

Zone 3/009/1 (NA) covers approximately 4.3 ha but contains zero building centroids in the 2026-05-01 snapshot.

This could be: (a) a newly designated zone over undeveloped land — legitimate; (b) an inventory lag; or (c) a polygon digitisation error. Compare against Vienna satellite imagery to distinguish the cases.

Orphan zones should not be conflated with the outside_any_zone building classification: the zone is real — it is the building list that may be incomplete relative to the zone.

No invalid-geometry buildings in the 2026-05-01 snapshot. sf::st_make_valid() resolved all geometries before the join. This story would fire if any upstream footprint polygon is self-intersecting or otherwise malformed.

Sanity Checks
Recommendations
What needs follow-up

  1. Straddles-boundary cases (0 buildings): The POC assigns one zone via centroid. Production should compute area-weighted overlap and store a list-column of all applicable zones with fractions.

  2. Multiple-zone cases (0 buildings): Audit each manually to determine whether overlapping zone polygons are intentional (layered rules) or a digitisation error. If intentional, the data model must support multiple simultaneous zone assignments per building.

  3. Orphan zones (34): Cross-reference each orphan polygon against current satellite imagery and planning documents to classify as

    1. legitimate undeveloped land, (b) inventory lag, or (c) polygon error.

  4. District assignment: The district column is NA for all buildings in this POC. Production should perform a secondary spatial join against the Vienna district boundary layer (BEZIRKSGRENZEOGD) to populate this field.

What production should add
  • Area-weighted overlap: Replace centroid join with full footprint intersection to compute exact overlap fractions per zone.
  • List-column schema: Allow multiple (zone_id, zone_type, overlap_fraction) tuples per building — required for straddlers and multi-zone buildings.
  • Address geocoding fallback: For buildings with invalid geometry, fall back to address-based geocoding before marking as invalid.
  • Snapshot refresh pipeline: Automate SNAPSHOT_DATE bumping and re-fetching via a targets pipeline target.
  • pointblank data contract: Convert these sanity checks into a formal pointblank agent with alerting on refresh.
Remote duckplyr query (Stage 2 preview)
Stage 2 architecture notes
Parquet on GitHub Pages

The snapshot Parquet files are now committed to docs/data/ and served by GitHub Pages at:

https://johngavin.github.io/acd_area_climate_design/data/

The load_acd_data() function supports two modes:

source Reads from Speed Network
"local" (default) inst/extdata/ (committed) Instant None
"remote" GitHub Pages via DuckDB httpfs ~1–2 s HTTP range requests

Why HTTP range requests are efficient: DuckDB reads only the byte ranges needed for the query (predicate / projection pushdown). A count(link_status) query downloads only the link_status column bytes — typically < 1 KB from a 30 KB Parquet file.

Stage 3 upgrade path: Replace REMOTE_BASE_URL in R/snapshot.R with an HuggingFace hf://datasets/... or S3/R2 URL when the dataset outgrows GitHub Pages limits (100 MB file cap, 1 GB repo cap).
